Thought: Aniline is a compound with the formula C6H5NH2. It consists of a benzene ring (which makes it aromatic) with an amino group (-NH2) attached to it. This structure makes aniline an aromatic amine. Aromatic refers to the benzene ring structure, and amine refers to the nitrogen-containing functional group.

Let's check the options:
A. Aldehydes - These have a -CHO group, which aniline doesn't have
B. Aromatic amines - This matches aniline's structure (benzene ring + amino group)
C. Carboxylic acids - These have a -COOH group, which aniline doesn't have
D. Ketones - These have a C=O group within a carbon chain, which aniline doesn't have
Final Answer: Aniline belongs to the class of compounds known as aromatic amines because it consists of a benzene ring (aromatic structure) with an amino group (-NH2) attached to it.
